messages:
oncall-bot: URGENT: Correctable ECC and repeated Xid driver resets observed in gpu-pool-4. Paging on-call: @sylvia
sylvia: seeing a spike of Xid 13 and 31 across gpu-04/gpu-07/gpu-09. Multiple driver resets and several containers restarting. tagging infra and runtime.
matt: grabbed kube logs from gpu-07 node:
```
[2026-03-15T03:11:54Z] NVRM: Xid (13): PID 4123: Xid error, resetting channel
[2026-03-15T03:11:55Z] kernel: Memory cgroup out of memory: Kill process 4123 (runtime) score 985
[2026-03-15T03:11:56Z] containerd: container exited with status 137
```
matt: appears host memory pressure + repeated driver resets leading to container OOMs. suspect kvcache churn.
chen: uploading nv-host and nvml dumps to /var/tmp/triage. nvidia-smi shows ECC correctable rising to ~100/min on gpu-07. NVML reports frequent resets.
leo: initiating immediate cordon/drain of gpu-07 and gpu-04 to prevent scheduling of new pods. running:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-07
kubectl drain gpu-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force\```
leo: will shift critical inference pods to fallback pool.
sre_lead: agree. Prioritize /redwood/gpt-serve and high-availability inference routes. Mark pool as degraded in routing config.
ops_bot: automated mitigation: route-fallback engaged -> shift 65% traffic to fallback-pool-a, 35% to dedicated-spare. Autoscaler disabled for quarantined nodes.
emily: drafting a short customer update for the bridge. will post after we confirm the isolation steps.
customer_bridge: created incident INC-431234 at https://redwood.example.com/incidents/INC-431234. Inviting SRE, Infra, Support.
sylvia: quick impact estimate: ~6% of live inference calls returned transient 5xx between 03:12-03:20 UTC. Most retried successfully by router. No evidence of corrupted model outputs.
matt: runtime excerpt before crash:
```
2026-03-15T03:12:16Z runtime: kvcache reserve failed: unable to allocate 1.1G
2026-03-15T03:12:17Z runtime: falling back to direct allocation, increasing host RSS
```
matt: kvcache reinitialization after reset seems to trigger host memory spikes.
chen: per-GPU corrected ECC counters:
- gpu-04: 0 -> 130/min (spike)
- gpu-07: 0 -> 98/min
- gpu-09: steady 3/min baseline
chen: also seeing NVML quiescent resets on gpu-07.
leo: attempted a soft nv-host restart + nvidia-smi --gpu-reset on gpu-07, reset refused remotely. escalating to hardware.
ops_bot: attempted automated soft-reset failed; escalating to on-prem field ops.
hardware: field ops standing by. can perform remote powercycle and reseat if remote reset fails. ETA 15m.
sre_lead: interim config change: apply KV_CACHE soft cap to reduce peak allocations for risky routes. set KV_CACHE_LIMIT=512M for /redwood/gpt-serve via config map patch. Also add a circuit-breaker on large-prefix routes to avoid cascading retries.
sylvia: applying KV cache cap now:
```
kubectl -n infra patch cm runtime-config --patch '{"data":{"KV_CACHE_LIMIT":"512M"}}'
```
emily: posted initial customer note on the incident bridge: "We are seeing driver resets on a subset of GPU hosts causing transient 5xxs. Traffic has been rerouted and affected hosts are being isolated. We will update within 2 hours or sooner." :information_source:
support: tagging impacted tenants and collecting escalation requests.
chen: driver dumps show predominant Xid codes: 13 (ECC correctable) and 31 (memory access), occasional 59. pattern suggests ECC correction saturation triggering NV driver channel resets.
matt: container OOMs are downstream of host memory surge after cache re-warm. runtime doesn't appear to be corrupted prior to kill.
sre_lead: action items:
- leo: finish drain + attempt controlled reboot of gpu-07 and gpu-04 (ETA 20m)
- chen: continue NVML/nv-host log collection, capture dmesg and oopses
- matt: extract per-container memory profiles and produce a minimal repro traffic pattern to exercise the kvcache
- emily: customer comms and cadence updates at :30 and EOD
- hardware: prepare for remote powercycle and possible GPU swap
leo: ack. starting node maintenance sequence in 2m, will report progress.
ops_bot: metrics: error-rate dropped from 6% -> 1.1% after route-fallback at 03:16 UTC. Request latency slightly increased on fallback pool.
sylvia: enable temporary retry caps on inbound routers to block retry storms in case of further resets.
chen: post-reboot nv-host log snippet from gpu-07:
```
[2026-03-15T03:25:08Z] nv-host: reinit attempt failed: ECC hardware flag persistent
[2026-03-15T03:25:12Z] kernel: parity errors detected on mmio region, escalating
```
hardware: performed remote powercycle and reseat of GPU on gpu-07 at 03:33 UTC. ECC error-rate dropped from ~120/min -> ~4/min after reseat. Running validation under quarantine for 12m.
leo: after reseat and reboot, performing slow-ramp inference test inside quarantine. observed one minor reset at 03:46 but no container OOMs.
sre_lead: decision: keep affected hosts quarantined for extended observation (4 hours). If ECC reappears above threshold, schedule full hardware replacement. Mark incident as mitigated for customer impact and continue monitoring.
emily: posted update to customers at 03:50 UTC: "We have isolated affected hosts and rerouted traffic; error rates have dropped significantly. We will continue to monitor and provide an RCA." :thumbsup:
customer_bridge: customers acknowledged; one customer requested detailed logs and timeline for RCA.
sre_lead: post-incident follow-ups to include:
- full RCA (hypothesis: hardware degradation causing ECC saturation combined with kvcache re-warm on heavy prefix workloads)
- replace failing GPU if ECC recurrence is observed
- implement KV_CACHE hysteresis and soft limit in runtime to prevent host OOM cascade
- add alert: per-GPU ECC corrected rate > 50/min triggers immediate quarantine automation
- add early detection for rapid increase in kvcache allocations per pod
- consider auto-throttle on heavy prefix routes
sylvia: closing active paging for now. keeping this thread for ops notes and postmortem inputs. thanks all. :heart:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> nodes quarantined; traffic rerouted. Incident status: monitoring. Incident ID INC-431234
